features.name: is_high_glucose
features.description: Boolean indicator for high plasma glucose levels, providing a direct split point for tree models.
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows tree models to immediately isolate individuals with elevated glucose, a primary physiological indicator.

features.name: bmi_category
features.description: Ordinal bucketing of BMI (mass) into standard clinical categories (underweight, normal, overweight, obese).
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a monotonic ordinal feature that groups similar body mass profiles, reducing the number of splits needed by the tree.

features.name: age_pregnancy_interaction
features.description: Ratio of pregnancies to age, capturing the frequency of pregnancies over the patient's adult lifespan.
features.expected_model_benefit: Exposes the density of pregnancies relative to age, which may be more informative than either feature independently.

features.name: insulin_glucose_ratio
features.description: Ratio of serum insulin to plasma glucose, a simple proxy for insulin production relative to circulating sugar.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the physiological relationship between insulin and glucose, providing a continuous interaction term for the model.

features.name: is_blood_pressure_abnormal
features.description: Boolean indicator for diastolic blood pressure outside the typical normal range (60-90 mm Hg).
features.expected_model_benefit: Groups both hypotensive and hypertensive individuals into a single abnormal category for efficient tree splitting.

features.name: metabolic_syndrome_risk_score
features.description: Semantic assessment of metabolic syndrome risk based on the combination of BMI, blood pressure, and glucose levels, outputting a continuous risk score.
features.expected_model_benefit: Synthesizes multiple physiological measurements into a single holistic risk score, capturing complex non-linear relationships.

features.name: pedigree_risk_bucket
features.description: Ordinal bucketing of the diabetes pedigree function to group individuals by genetic risk magnitude.
features.expected_model_benefit: Transforms a continuous genetic risk score into discrete ordinal steps, which are often easier for tree models to split on robustly.

features.name: missing_biometrics_count
features.description: Count of zero values across biological measurements where zero typically indicates a missing value rather than a true physiological state.
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows the model to explicitly learn patterns associated with missing data, which may correlate with specific patient demographics or data collection practices.

features.name: glucose_bmi_product
features.description: Multiplicative interaction between plasma glucose and BMI.
features.expected_model_benefit: Highlights individuals who have both high glucose and high BMI, creating a strong interaction feature for the tree.

features.name: age_group
features.description: Ordinal bucketing of age into distinct life stages.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a coarse-grained demographic feature, allowing the tree to make broad splits before fine-tuning on exact age.

features.name: insulin_resistance_proxy
features.description: Semantic judgment estimating the severity of insulin resistance by evaluating the interplay between skin fold thickness, BMI, and insulin levels.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a high-level physiological interpretation of raw measurements, giving the model access to domain-like expertise.

features.name: adjusted_glucose
features.description: Plasma glucose level adjusted by the logarithm of age, accounting for natural metabolic changes over time.
features.expected_model_benefit: Normalizes glucose levels against age, potentially revealing abnormal glucose levels that are masked by age-related baselines.
